Readings

I. Foundations

Session 1: Introduction: What Is an Emerging Technology and Does It Matter?

  • Rotolo, Daniele, Diana Hicks, and Ben Martin. 2015. âWhat Is an Emerging Technology?â Research Policy 44 (10): 1827â1843.
  • Horowitz, Michael C. 2020. âDo Emerging Military Technologies Matter for International Politics?â (PDF). Annual Review of Political Science 23 (1): 385â400.

Session 2: Thinking About the Future

Read

  • Wack, Pierre. 1985. âScenarios: Shooting the RapidsâHow Medium-Term Analysis Illuminated the Power of Scenarios for Shell Management.â Harvard Business Review (NovemberâDecember 1985): 139â150.
  • Royal Dutch Shell. 2012. â40 Years of Shell Scenarios.â (PDF). Skim 1â39.
  • National Intelligence Council. 2021. Global Trends 2040: A More Contested World. (PDF). Read pages 54â65 and 108â119.

Watch

  • âNavigating an Uncertain Future.â Shell Scenarios. YouTube.
  • âWindows on the Future: Modelling Scenarios.â Shell Scenarios. YouTube.

Session 3: Key Tenets of International Relations Theory

  • Levy, Jack, and William R. Thompson. 2010. Causes of War. Wiley-Blackwell. Pages 28â43 and 63â70. [Preview with Google Books]
  • Gvosdev, Nikolas K., Jessica D. Blankshain, and David A. Cooper. 2019. Decision-Making in American Foreign Policy: Translating Theory into Practice. Cambridge University Press. Pages 162â180 and 88â114. [Preview with Google Books]

Session 4: Conceptualizing Innovation

  • Bower, Joseph L., and Clayton Christensen. 1995, âDisruptive Technologies: Catching the Wave.â Harvard Business Review 73 (1): 43â53.
  • Christensen, Clayton. 2011. The Innovatorâs Dilemma. HarperCollins. Chapter 11.
  • Rosen, Stephen P. 1988. âNew Ways of War: Understanding Military Innovation.â International Security 13 (1): 134â168.
  • Kuo, Kendrick. 2024. âHow to think about Risks in U.S. Military Innovation.â Survival 66 (1): 85â98.

Session 5: Diffusion of Innovations

  • Rogers, Everett. 2003. Diffusion of Innovations. Free Press. Chapters 1 and 6. [Preview with Google Books]
  • Horowitz, Michael. 2010. The Diffusion of Military Power: Causes and Consequences for International Politics. Princeton University Press. Chapter 2. [Preview with Google Books]
  • Adamsky, Dima. 2010. The Culture of Military Innovation. Stanford University Press. Introduction and Chapter 1. [Preview with Google Books]
  • Cronin, Audrey Kurth. 2019. Power to the People. Oxford University Press. Pages 19â35. [Preview with Google Books]

Sessions 6 and 7: Technologyâs Effects on International Relations

  • Fritsch, Stefan. 2011. âTechnology and Global Affairs.â International Studies Perspectives 12 (1): 27â45.
  • Levy, Jack S. 1984. âThe Offensive/Defensive Balance of Military Technology: A Theoretical and Historical Analysis.â International Studies Quarterly 28 (2): 219â238.
  • van Creveld, Martin. 1991. Technology and War: From 2000 B.C. to the Present. Free Press. Pages 311â321.
  • Krepinevich, Andrew. 1994. âCavalry to Computer: The Pattern of Military Revolutions.â The National Interest 37: 30â42.
  • Cohen, Eliot. 2004. âChange and Transformation in Military Affairs.â Journal of Strategic Studies 27 (3): 395â407.
  • Gray, Colin. 1993. Weapons Donât Make War. University of Kansas Press. Chapter 1.
  • Ellis, John. 1981. The Social History of the Machine Gun. Arno Press. Chapters 1 and 7. [Preview with Google Books]

II. Historical Innovations

Session 8: Dynamite

  • Schneider, Jacquelyn, and Julia Macdonald. 2023. âLooking Back to Look Forward: Autonomous Systems, Military Revolutions, and the Importance of Cost.â Journal of Strategic Studies 47(2): 162â184.
  • Cronin, Audrey Kurth. 2019. Power to the People. Oxford University Press. Pages 61â125.

Session 9: Stealth and Secret Innovations

  • âHarold Brownâs âInvisibleâ Aircraft.â 2006. Air & Space Forces Magazine. August 1.
  • Westwick, Peter. 2020. Stealth: The Secret Contest to Invent Invisible Aircraft. Oxford University Press. Pages 1â30; 181â198. [Preview with Google Books]
  • Green, Brendan R., and Austin Long. 2020. âConceal or Reveal? Managing Clandestine Military Capabilities in Peacetime Competition.â International Security 44(3): 48â83.

III. Emerging Technologies and Their Security Implications (Thinking About Innovation as an Independent Variable)

Information, Intelligence, and Decision-Making

Session 10: Information Asymmetries, Big Data, and the Democratization of Information

  • Fearon, James. 1995. âRationalist Explanations for War.â International Organization 49 (3). Pages 379â386 and 390â401.
  • Berman, Eli, Jacob Shapiro, and Joseph Felter. 2019. Small Wars, Big Data: The Information Revolution in ModernÂ Conflict. Princeton University Press. Pages 82â108.
  • Ball, James. 2018. âHow a Guy with a Camera Outsmarted the United States.â The Atlantic. December 28.
  • Hsu, Jeremy. 2018. âThe Strava Heat Map and the End of Secrets.â Wired. January 29.

Session 11: Delegating the âDisclosure DecisionââCommercial Satellites

  • Carnegie, Allison, and Austin Carson. 2019. âThe Trump Administration is Revealing U.S. Intelligence Operations. Is it Revealing too Much?â The Washington Post. June 20
  • Albright, David, Sarah Burkhard, and Allison Lach. 2018. âCommercial Satellite Imagery Analysis for Countering Nuclear Proliferation.â Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences 46 (1): 99â121.
  • Lin-Greenberg, Erik, and Theo Milonopoulos. 2022. âPrivate Eyes in the Sky: Emerging Technology and the Political Consequences of Eroding Government Secrecy.â Journal of Conflict Resolution 65 (6).
  • Spend some time exploring Tearline.mil.Â 

Sessions 12 and 13: Artificial Intelligence

  • Lindsay, Jon R. 2023. âWar Is from Mars, AI Is from Venus: Rediscovering the Institutional Context of Military Automation.â Texas National Security Review 7(1): 29â47.
  • Kania, Elsa. 2019. âChinese Military Innovation in the AI Revolution.â The RUSI Journal 164 (5â6): 26â34.
  • Brose, Christian. 2020. The Kill Chain. Hachette. Chapter 7.
  • Bleicher, Ariel. 2017. âDemystifying the Black Box That Is AI.â Scientific American. August 9.
  • Brown, Tristan G., Alexander Statman, and Celine Sui. 2021. âPublic Debate on Facial Recognition Technologies in China.â MIT Schwarzman SERC Case Studies.

Optional

  • âFinal Report.â (PDF) National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence. 2021.

Session 14: In-Class Midterm

  • No readings assigned

Emerging Technologies, Stability, and the Use of Force

Sessions 15 and 16: Internet, Social Media, and Domestic Stability

  • Kuran, Timur. 1991. âNow out of Never: The Element of Surprise in the East European Revolution of 1989.â World Politics 44 (1): 7â48. (Read 7â13 and 16â25, skim other pages.)
  • Nugent, Elizabeth R., and Chantal Berman. 2018. âCtrl-Alt-Revolt? Online and Off-Line Networks During the 2011 Egyptian Uprising.â Middle East Law and Governance 10 (1): 59â90.
  • Tufekci, Zeynep. 2018. Twitter and Tear Gas. Yale University Press. Chapter 3. [Preview with Google Books]
  • King, Gary, Jennifer Pan, and Margaret Roberts. 2014. âReverse-Engineering Censorship in China: Randomized Experimentation and Participant Observation.â Science 345 (6199): 1â10.
  • Gohdes, Anita. 2020. âRepression Technology: Internet Accessibility and State Violence.â American Journal of Political Science 64 (3): 488â503.

Recommended

  • Hass, Benjamin. 2019. âThe New Battle in Hong Kong Isnât on the Streets; Itâs in the Apps.â MIT Technology Review. September 10.

Session 17: Social Media and the International Stage

  • Kreps, Sarah. 2020. Social Media and International Relations. Cambridge University Press. Chapters 1â4. [Preview with Google Books]
  • Williams, Heather, and Alexi Drew. 2020. Escalation by Tweet. (PDF). Kings College.Â 
  • Harris, Benjamin, and Erik Lin-Greenberg. 2024. âCheap Tweets: Crisis Signaling in the Age of Twitter.â International Studies Quarterly 68 (2).
  • Green-Riley, Naima, Dominika Kruszewksa-Eduardo, and Ze Fu. 2022. âTeargas and Selfie Cams: Foreign Protests and Media in the Digital Age.â Journal of Experimental Political Science 9 (2): 203â215.

Recommended

  • Lewis, Jeffrey. 2018. The 2020 Commission Report on the North Korean Nuclear Attacks Against the United States: A Speculative Novel. Mariner Books. Chapter 3.

Sessions 18 and 19: Cyber Warfare

  • Branch, Jordan. 2021. âWhatâs in a Name? Metaphors and Cybersecurity.â International Organization 75 (1): 39â70.
  • Healey, Jason, and Robert Jervis. 2020. âThe Escalation Inversion and Other Oddities of Situational Cyber Stability.â Texas National Security Review 3 (4): 30â53.
  • Healey, Jason. 2024. âCyber Effects in Warfare: Categorizing the Where, What, and Why.â Texas National Security Review 7 (4): 37â50.
  • Kreps, Sarah, and Debak Das. 2017. âWarring from the Virtual to the Real: Assessing the Publicâs Threshold for War over Cyber Security.â Research & Politics 4 (2): 1â8.
  • Kostyuk, Nadiya, and Yuri Zhukov. 2019. âInvisible Digital Front: Can Cyber Attacks Shape Battlefield Events?â Journal of Conflict Resolution 63 (2): 317â347.

Session 20: Drones and Autonomous Weapon Systems

  • Byman, Daniel. 2013. âWhy Drones Work.â Foreign Affairs 92 (4): 32â43.
  • Cronin, Audrey Kruth. 2013. âWhy Drones Fail.â Foreign Affairs 92 (4): 44â54.
  • Chavez, Kerry, and Ori Swed. 2023. âEmulating Underdogs: Tactical Drones in the Russia Ukraine War.â Contemporary Security Policy 44 (4): 592â605.
  • Dinstein, Yoram. 2004. The Conduct of Hostilities under the Law of International Armed Conflict. Cambridge University Press. Chapter 3.Â 
  • Lin-Greenberg, Erik. 2019. âGame of Drones: What Experimental Wargames Reveal About Drones and Escalation.â War on the Rocks. January 10.
  • âDepartment of Defense Directive 3000.09: Autonomy in Weapon Systems.â (PDF). Department of Defense. January 25, 2023.
  • Scharre, Paul. 2018. Army of None. W.W. Norton. Pages 11â58.

From the Lab to the Front Lines

Session 21: Biotech

  • Koblentz, Gregory. 2003. âPathogens as Weapons: The International Security Implications of Biological Warfare.â International Security 28 (3): 84â122.
  • Vogel, Kathleen, and Sonia Ben Ouagrham-Gormley. 2018. âAnticipating Emerging Biotechnology Threats: A Case Study of CRISPR.â Politics and the Life Sciences 37 (2): 203â219.
  • Brent, Roger, Greg McKelvey, and Jason Matheny. 2024. âThe New Bioweapons: How Synthetic Biology Could Destabilize the World.â Foreign Affairs 103(5): 148â159.
  • Palmer, Megan, Francis Fukuyama, and David Relman. 2015. âA More Systematic Approach to Biological Risk.â Science 350 (6267): 1471â1473.

Recommended

  • Smith, Frank L. 2011. âA Casualty of Kinetic Warfare: Military Research, Development, and Acquisition for Biodefense.â Security Studies 20 (4): 663â696.
  • George, Asha. 2019. âThe National Security Implications of Cyberbiosecurity.â Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology 7(51): 1â4.

Session 22: Additive Manufacturing

  • Gershenfeld, Neil. 2012. âHow to Make Almost Anything: The Digital Fabrication Revolution.â Foreign Affairs 91 (6): 43â57.
  • Price, Jaren K., Miranda C. La Bash, and Bart Land. 2019. â3D Printing for Joint Agile Operations.â (PDF) Joint Force Quarterly 95 (4): 92â99.
  • Kroenig, Matthew, and Tristan Volpe. 2015. â3-D Printing the Bomb? The Nuclear Nonproliferation Challenge.â Washington Quarterly 38 (3): 7â19.
  • Thong, Calvin Seah Ser, and Choo Wei Wen. 2016. â3D PrintingâRevolutionising Military Operations.â Pointer 42 (2): 35â46.

Session 23: Everyday Technologies and International Relations

  • Adler-Nissen, Rebecca, and Alena Drieschova. 2019. âTrack-Change Diplomacy: Technology, Affordances, and the Practice of International Negotiations.â International Studies Quarterly 63 (3): 531â45.
  • Chen, John, Emily Walz, Brian Lafferty, Joe Mc Reynolds, Kieran Green, Jonathan Ray, and James Mulvenon. 2018. âChinaâs Internet of Things.â (PDF). U.S. China Economic and Security Review Commission. Pages 103â121.
  • Weber, Valentin. 2023. âChinaâs Smart Cities and the Future of Geopolitics.â German Council on Foreign Relations.
  • âCybersecurity Best Practices for Smart Cities.â (PDF). 2023. US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Â 

IV. Application

Sessions 24 and 25: Student Presentations

  • No readings assigned
